stories.title: Russia / Ukraine / NATO
stories.detail: Above its own baseline: 12 headlines against a normal of 22.0. That is a change, not just continuing coverage.
stories.why: Two channels: haven demand, and the structural one - sanctions on Russian reserves in 2022 taught central banks that dollar reserves can be frozen, which is a large part of why official-sector gold buying has been so persistent since.
stories.counterweight: Day-to-day headlines are largely priced. The structural bid shows up in central bank demand data, not in a day's price action.
stories.duration: Headlines: days. The reserve-diversification effect: years, and it is arguably the single biggest reason gold has re-rated.
stories.spoken_why: The day to day headlines are priced, but sanctions on reserves are why central banks keep buying gold.
stories.read: Broadly consistent, though Gold, S&P 500, Silver are not playing along. One asset out of line is usually its own story; several is a reason to doubt the read.

stories.title: US / Israel – Iran
stories.detail: 9 headlines, which is about its normal of 42.0 after 25 days running. Continuing coverage rather than escalation - gold has priced this.
stories.why: The one flashpoint that hits gold through every channel at once. Safe-haven bid on the headline, Treasuries bid so nominal and real yields fall, and - uniquely - a credible threat to the Strait of Hormuz spikes crude, which lifts inflation expectations. Roughly a fifth of seaborne oil passes through that strait.
stories.counterweight: The dollar is also a haven, so risk-off bids the dollar too and cancels part of gold's gain. This is why some escalation days produce a far smaller gold move than the headlines imply.
stories.duration: Days. Gold spikes on the exchange of fire and gives most of it back within a week unless the oil disruption is real and sustained, because only then does it reach the Fed's reaction function.

headlines.summary: Russian attacks in recent days on on Ukraine’s two largest cities have again killed and injured civilians, damaged homes and civilian infrastructure, the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) said on Tuesday.

headlines.title: Girl rescued from flaming apartment after Israeli attack on Gaza
headlines.summary: Civilians rushed to rescue a girl trapped in a burning apartment after an Israeli attack struck a building in Gaza City.

headlines.title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI
headlines.summary: Sir Ken McCallum says operations to tackle terrorism and state threats are now roughly of an "equal scale".

geo.caveat: Each flashpoint is measured against its own trailing 30-day median, so a long-running conflict does not sit at maximum forever. This measures how loud a story is relative to its own normal - not what will happen.

profile.name: FOMC Member Speaks
profile.what: Remarks from a regional Fed president or governor.
profile.why_gold: Mostly background, but a known hawk turning dovish - or the reverse - is a genuine signal, and voting members matter more than non-voters.
profile.watch: Whether the speaker votes this year, and whether they are departing from their usual stance.
profile.gotchas: Several speakers a day is normal and almost always noise. Treat as background unless the tone genuinely shifts.

profile.name: Consumer Price Index
profile.what: Headline and core consumer inflation, month on month and year on year. Released 13:30 UK (08:30 ET).
profile.who: Bureau of Labor Statistics, monthly, usually mid-month
profile.why_gold: The most reliable single driver of Fed expectations, and therefore of gold. A hot print lifts real yields and the dollar and knocks gold; a cool one does the reverse.
profile.watch: Core m/m is what the market trades - headline is noisier because of energy. A 0.1pp surprise against forecast is enough to move the metal.
profile.gotchas: Gold's first move is sometimes reversed within the hour if the internals (shelter, supercore) contradict the headline.
